subject: biology

moments.title: Helmholtz on muscle
moments.body: Helmholtz measures muscle contraction times and energy use, founding muscle physiology. He shows it follows thermodynamic laws — no 'vital force'.

moments.title: Sliding filament theory
moments.who: H. E. Huxley & J. Hanson; A. F. Huxley & R. Niedergerke
moments.body: Two papers, in the same issue of Nature, propose the sliding-filament theory. Two filaments — thin actin and thick myosin — slide past each other during contraction.
moments.takeaway: Muscle contracts by molecular sliding, not coiling.

moments.title: Huxley's swinging cross-bridge
moments.body: Andrew Huxley proposes the cross-bridge cycle: myosin heads attach to actin, pivot, detach, reattach further along. ATP powers each cycle.
moments.takeaway: A motor protein walking along an actin track.

moments.title: Single-molecule motors
moments.body: Optical traps observe single myosin molecules taking steps along actin. The motor walks ~5 nm per ATP. Cytoskeletal motors (kinesin, dynein, myosin) are now studied at single-molecule scale.
moments.takeaway: Biology's molecular motors can be watched, atom by atom.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Muscle disease therapies target the cross-bridge cycle (e.g. mavacamten for HCM). Cytoskeletal motors are tracked in living cells. Optogenetic control of motors is being developed.
now.open_questions: Can synthetic biology engineer molecular motors with novel cargo?

reflection: Two competing groups published sliding-filament theory back-to-back in 1954. How does scientific competition shape discovery?
